name: Tretinoin + microneedling stack
lead: The tretinoin plus microneedling stack is a skin-care protocol discussed in appearance forums that combines a topical retinoid (tretinoin) with microneedling, typically with a derma roller, aiming at acne scars, texture and aging signs.

Each component has its own literature. Topical tretinoin is described as the most extensively studied retinoid for photoaging, with improvement usually taking weeks to months, and irritation is its main adverse effect [1]. Microneedling has been used for scarring and acne [2]. Neither reference describes the two as a combined protocol, and no trial of the combination was identified for this article.
infobox: Prescription-only in US, UK, EU and Australia

paras: Tretinoin is a retinoid used for comedonal and inflammatory acne and photoaging. It was approved by the FDA for acne in 1971 and is prescription-only in several countries [1]. Common adverse effects of the topical form are redness, swelling and irritation, and increased sun sensitivity [1].

Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, repeatedly punctures the skin with sterile needles. It has been used for scarring and acne, and research on combinations such as platelet-rich plasma is described as ongoing [2]. Health officials have warned about infection risks when related services are performed without infection-control training [2].

Forum users describe using tretinoin on a nightly schedule and microneedling at intervals, with the belief that the two reinforce collagen stimulation. Protocol details were not drawn from the sources reviewed and are not given here. Dermatology references on each component do not address how they interact, and skin irritation from both together has not been characterized in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: Tretinoin approved by the FDA for acne [1].

card.summary: A forum protocol pairing prescription tretinoin with microneedling for scars and texture; each part has evidence, the combination has none found.
card.note: Tretinoin is Rx-only; both parts can irritate skin; no combination trials found.

quick.overview:
This stack combines a topical retinoid, tretinoin, with microneedling, usually at home with a roller, for scars, texture and aging signs.

Tretinoin is well studied for acne and photoaging and microneedling has been used for scarring, but no trial of the two together was found.
quick.mechanism: Tretinoin is a retinoid that acts on skin cell turnover and collagen over weeks to months. Microneedling makes controlled punctures intended to stimulate repair.
quick.risks: Tretinoin commonly causes irritation and sun sensitivity and is prescription-only in many countries. Microneedling carries infection concerns when done without proper hygiene.
